thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated tail latency observed for inference-prod streaming endpoints (p99 spike, streaming stalls). Paging events increased; cache hit rate for kvbucket-17 prefix group dropped. Auto-mitigation not applied because policy requires on-call confirmation. :warning:

jordan-oncall: seeing it in dashboard — p95 ~220ms -> 450ms, p99 up to 2.1s for streaming responses. error rate stable, but a lot of stalled streams (idle token generation).

sara-ml: we rolled the prefix-seed rotation earlier (00:15 UTC) for kvbucket-17 to improve distribution. suspect that changed hash mapping causing a lot of prefix misses. hit-rate graph shows drop from ~92% to ~18% for short-prefixes.

mike-infra: confirming logs show a spike of cache-miss-throughput and backend paging bursts. paging queue length for shard-7 jumped 6x.

ops-bot: Automated note: incident created, severity=P2, pager sent to @jordan-oncall.

jordan-oncall: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) revert seed rotation if safe; 2) increase prefix cache TTL temporarily or enable permissive cache-bypass fallback to avoid stalls; 3) route heavy streaming traffic to dedicated pool. Thoughts?

sara-ml: revert is the cleanest if we can do it fast. we need to check compatibility of seed rollback with currently-warmed caches. if we revert, some cache entries will be invalid and cause another spike unless we also enable soft-warm.

tina-sre: propose quick soft-mitigation: set prefix cache to "permissive" mode (serve from origin if cache miss, don't block stream), and increase in-memory KVCACHE TTL to 5m from 30s. That should reduce blocking while we decide on revert.

luke-prod: pushing permissive mode would be low-risk. also we can temporarily raise streaming concurrency for that route to drain paging backlog.

mike-infra: I can flip permissive mode. doing a quick check: current config for kvbucket-17 -> {seed: 0x9af3, mode: strict, ttl: 30s}. will change to {mode: permissive, ttl: 300s} for shard-7 only.

jordan-oncall: go ahead mike. make the change in staging-first? I'm fine with direct prod if timeout is low. ping here when done.

mike-infra: applying change now. patch:
```
PATCH /config/cache/kvbucket-17
{ "shard": 7, "mode": "permissive", "ttl_seconds": 300 }
```
Rolling update to 3 nodes (shard-7).

ops-bot: config-change accepted, rollout started (change-id: cfg-20260314-942).

mike-infra: nodes updated. observing metrics...

sara-ml: hit-rate climbing slowly back to ~65% for short-prefixes. p99 trending down to 700-900ms. streaming stalls reduced. early signs good.

jordan-oncall: good. still need to validate customer impact. Luke — can you correlate customer-facing error reports and 5xxs?

luke-prod: checking support logs: 3 customers filed complaints about slow responses between 00:20-00:40 UTC, total ~0.8% of active requests; no increase in 5xxs, mostly extreme latency/streaming timeouts. I opened a ticket for the two enterprise customers that might have been affected.

incident-bot: PagerDuty event linked: PD-INC-7744.

sara-ml: root cause hypothesis: seed rotation altered prefix->shard mapping for a subset of short prefixes used heavily by streaming prompt templates. those prefixes had high locality in old mapping resulting in high cache hit rates. rotation increased entropy causing many cold misses and synchronous backend fetches -> paging bursts -> tail latency.

tina-sre: agreed. two follow-ups: 1) add canary for prefix-seed rotations that simulates traffic and measures projected hit-rate delta; 2) add automatic fallback to permissive mode when cache hit-rate drops below 40% and paging queue growth > 3x.

jordan-oncall: +1 on both. also add a rolling-warm step to rotation: sample top-k prefixes, pre-populate new mapping caches before cutover.

mike-infra: logging some debug snippets from shard-7 at peak:
```
[2026-03-14T00:22:11Z] cache_miss prefix="/p/short/abcd" shard=7 fetch_time=452ms
[2026-03-14T00:22:12Z] paging_enqueue shard=7 len=142 inflight=18
[2026-03-14T00:23:02Z] stream_wait start prefix="/p/short/efgh" duration=1.9s
```

luke-prod: prometheus queries we used:
```
# p99 latency for streaming route
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(streaming_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
# prefix cache hit-rate for kvbucket-17
sum(rate(kvcache_prefix_hits_total{bucket="kvbucket-17"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_prefix_requests_total{bucket="kvbucket-17"}[5m]))
```

jordan-oncall: can we quantify percentage of total traffic routed through the affected prefix set? need to know blast radius before full revert.

sara-ml: we sampled traffic: ~6% of overall requests hit the particular short-prefix namespace but they represent ~28% of streaming p99 weight (they're heavy token generators).

tina-sre: considering blast radius, we should not revert immediately without warming. plan: keep permissive mode + increased TTL for 30m, run background pre-warm for top-5K prefixes into new mapping, then schedule controlled revert to previous seed during low traffic window (3h).

mike-infra: starting pre-warm job now (prewarm-id: pw-1936). will stream top prefixes from analytics into the new mapping. job details:
```
prewarm --bucket kvbucket-17 --shard 7 --prefix-list top5k --concurrency 8
```
Estimated runtime ~12m.

ops-bot: Prewarm job pw-1936 started.

mike-infra: pre-warm finished. cache warm metrics show top prefixes warmed to ~95% occupancy for shard-7. paging queue length baseline restored.

sara-ml: with pre-warm, p99 back to ~320-420ms, p95 ~180-250ms. still higher than baseline but acceptable for now.

jordan-oncall: good work. escalate to post-incident review: include metrics pre/post rotation, canary failure, and suggested policy changes. I'll handoff to @tina-sre for overnight monitoring and follow-up. Anyone object?

luke-prod: no objections. I'll notify the two impacted customers and set expectation that we've mitigated and are stabilizing.

tina-sre: taking handoff. I'll keep permissive mode until 04:00 UTC and monitor. action items assigned to infra+ml+prod for RCA doc and playbook updates.

jordan-oncall: handing off: see ops-runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-rotation. On-call: @tina-sre until 04:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P3. Postmortem requested, owner: sara-ml. ETA for draft: 72h.

tina-sre: quick customer impact summary to include in postmortem: ~0.8% of requests experienced high latency between 00:20-00:40 UTC; no 5xx spike; two enterprise customers reported slow responses and were contacted.

sara-ml: will draft RCA and include the following remediation items: canary prewarm step, automatic permissive fallback, add rollout guard on seed rotations, and telemetry alert for rapid hit-rate drops (delta > 40% in 5m).

mike-infra: will create infra PR to implement permissive auto-fallback + prewarm job templating.

jordan-oncall: thanks team — great triage. leaving thread for follow-up. :thumbsup:

tina-sre: monitoring, closing handoff.
